subject: Civil Engineering
title: Timber: Engineering's Oldest Material
description: A quick, practical guide to Timber: Engineering's Oldest Material.

hook.text: Japanese temples built with wood have survived earthquakes for 1,400 years.

buildup.text: Wood is strong for its weight, renewable, and stores carbon throughout its life.

discovery.text: Glue-laminated timber stacks thin layers into beams stronger than solid logs.

twist.text: Large timber members char on the outside in a fire but stay strong inside.

climax.text: Cross-laminated timber buildings now reach 18 stories — rival steel high-rises.

punchline.text: The oldest building material is becoming the newest again.

quiz.question: Why does large timber perform surprisingly well in fires?
options: Wood is naturally fireproof when dried properly
The charred outer layer insulates the structural core inside
Timber buildings are always treated with fire-retardant chemicals

details.summary: Timber is a renewable structural material with excellent strength-to-weight ratio, natural beauty, and carbon storage benefits. Modern engineered timber products like glued-laminated beams, cross-laminated timber panels, and laminated veneer lumber overcome natural wood limitations.
details.whyItMatters: Timber construction is experiencing a renaissance as sustainability priorities grow. Mass timber buildings offer lower carbon footprints than concrete or steel equivalents while achieving comparable structural performance.
takeaways: Engineered timber products eliminate natural defects like knots and grain deviation
Cross-laminated timber uses alternating grain layers for two-way slab action
Timber stores carbon absorbed during tree growth, reducing building carbon footprint

faq.question: How do engineered timber products overcome natural wood's limitations?
faq.answer: Glued-laminated timber glues thin boards into large beams, spreading natural defects randomly so no single knot weakens the whole member. Cross-laminated timber alternates grain direction in layers, providing strength in two directions.

faq.question: How does mass timber perform in fire?
faq.answer: Large timber members char on the surface at a predictable rate of about 0.6 mm per minute. The char layer insulates the interior, maintaining structural capacity. A 200 mm CLT panel retains adequate strength after 2 hours of fire exposure. Steel, by contrast, rapidly loses strength in fire.
